item.title: Opening Statement before the House of Commons Standing Committee on Finance

rating.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem presented the rationale for a 25 basis point rate hike—the first since July 2023—bringing the policy rate to 2.5%, citing a deteriorated inflation outlook driven by elevated global oil prices and a modestly improved growth picture. CPI inflation is running around 3% and is projected to rise to 3.5% by year-end, remaining above 3% through much of 2027. The Bank signaled it would proceed carefully and take decisions meeting-by-meeting, leaving the door open to further hikes.
rating.stance_rationale: The statement is moderately hawkish: the Bank has just raised rates and explicitly noted 'there could be a need to raise the policy rate further,' while also acknowledging elevated uncertainty and a cautious, meeting-by-meeting approach that tempers the hawkish lean.
key_quotes: With elevated inflation expected to last longer and the economy showing resilience, Governing Council agreed that risks to inflation had increased and there was less scope for monetary accommodation.
There could be a need to raise the policy rate further, but given the uncertainties, we will proceed carefully.
